Home.firstMatchTitle: Five things that catch you out in your first match
Home.firstMatchLead: Habits from one title carry over badly into the others. Name pairings are collected in the term mapping guide.

Ward.label: Before you step into a bush
Ward.pitfall: The three games find enemies in completely different ways. Walk into the river on the wrong habit and you get collapsed on.
Ward.hok: No ward item exists. The roamer steps into the bush first, or throws a skill in to see what reacts.
Ward.wr: Everyone carries free wards, and the Sweeping Lens clears the enemy's.
Ward.mlbb: Step into a bush the enemy has no vision of and you vanish. Attack from inside and your position is given away.

Recall.label: Before you head home
Recall.pitfall: Low health sends you back to base. What you can do instead differs by title.
Recall.hok: Items are bought from anywhere on the map, so a recall is for healing.
Recall.wr: Shopping happens at the fountain only. Go right after you shove the wave into the tower.
Recall.mlbb: Small healing camps spawn in the first 30 to 40 seconds. Killing one restores health and mana without going home.

LastHit.label: Minion gold
LastHit.pitfall: Chipping minions down earns nothing. The item gap at ten minutes starts here.
LastHit.hok: Land the killing blow and you take roughly 1.5x what a minion dying beside you pays.
LastHit.wr: Gold lands only on the killing blow. Missed CS turns straight into an item deficit.
LastHit.mlbb: The gold lane pays the most. Harass the enemy but drop two minions and you are down on the trade.

Tower.label: Diving a tower
Tower.pitfall: Chase someone under their tower and the tower turns on you. Check the conditions before stepping in.
Tower.hok: Outer towers take 40% less damage for the first four minutes, and your damage to a tower drops 55% with no allied minions beside you.
Tower.wr: The standard early plan is to take the Rift Herald and send it charging into the tower.
Tower.mlbb: Outer turrets carry a shield for the first five minutes: 30% less damage taken, and 15% less for allies nearby.

Objective.label: Objective timers
Objective.pitfall: Objectives are the call to group up. Read the clock wrong and it is over before you arrive.
Objective.hok: The Overlord and the Tyrant both spawn at 4:00, and are replaced by Shadow versions at 10:00.
Objective.wr: Seven in all: four dragons, the Rift Herald, Baron Nashor and the Elder Dragon.
Objective.mlbb: The Turtle spawns at 2:00 and the Lord at 8:00. A killed Turtle returns two minutes later, and stops at 8:00.

GuideWhatIsMoba.title: What Makes MOBAs So Addictive? A Deep Dive into 5v5 Battles
GuideWhatIsMoba.intro: I uninstalled my first MOBA the same night. Five years and 2,000 hours later, here is my attempt to work out why a 5v5 genre that loses you eight games in ten is so hard to put down.
GuideWhatIsMoba.pageTitle: Five Years Deep in the MOBA Rabbit Hole
GuideWhatIsMoba.author: By HUB-GAME
leadParagraphs: Up front: a MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) is not a game I would cheerfully hand to just anyone with a "trust me, it's fun, give it a shot."

I still remember my first day in the genre. A friend talked me into installing it, and I could not tell you what was happening on screen. Some ability I never saw coming landed on me from somewhere off to the side, everything went grey, and a teammate typed: please just stay under the tower.
I uninstalled it that same night, fully convinced the whole thing was unfair garbage.
GuideWhatIsMoba.pullQuote: And then, a few days later, it surfaced out of nowhere: if I hadn't walked through that bush, I probably would have lived. I was clicking download again before I had really decided to.
GuideWhatIsMoba.leadOutro: That was the start of everything. I'm past 2,000 hours in the genre now. So here is my attempt to work out, from my own experience, why these games swallow so much of your time.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section1Heading: ■ Fifteen to twenty minutes a match, and the perfect high only lands once every ten
section1Setup: A MOBA match is five players against five, all tangled up on the same map. Everyone opens at level 1, farms minions for gold, and buys items to grow into the late game.

The correct play changes with every situation, and plenty of matches fall apart purely because nobody on the team is reading it the same way. Eight games out of ten I close the client annoyed, still stinging, still wondering why nobody rotated when I pinged.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section1Highlight: But in the other one or two, you get the impossible moment.
section1Payoff: Late game, the match already looking lost, no vision anywhere on the map, and the teamfight timing lands exactly right. Their main damage dealer goes down in the opening second, the ace follows, and a dead game flips.

The shaking hands and the rush that hits right after aren't something I've found in any action game or FPS. Once you've had that once, the eight losses stop reading as losses and turn into the setup for the next one. That, I think, is the genuinely dangerous part of this genre.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Heading: ■ Five roles, and one of them will fit you
GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Intro: The same way soccer has strikers and keepers, a MOBA team is built out of five roles.

roles.name: TOP:
roles.description: The far edge of the map, where you and your lane opponent trade blows for as long as it takes. It suits patient players who like a straight 1v1.

roles.name: MID:
roles.description: The center of the map, usually on a flashy assassin or mage. Made for players who want the spotlight and hold up under pressure.

roles.name: JUNGLE:
roles.description: No lane of your own. You clear the camps in the forest and look for gank windows. The role for people who like reading the whole map at once.

roles.name: ADC (Marksman):
roles.description: Weak in the early game, but once the gold is banked, you can shred the enemy team on auto-attacks alone. The team's main damage source in the late game.

roles.name: SUPPORT:
roles.description: Heals, shields, and vision for the rest of the team. It looks unglamorous, but the support is usually the one who decides when a teamfight starts.

GuideWhatIsMoba.section2Outro: Even if you start out sure your reflexes aren't good enough, you can still decide games from the jungle or by specializing on support. Finding the role that matches how your head already works is a real part of the appeal.
GuideWhatIsMoba.section3Heading: ■ Last thing, for anyone about to start
section3Paragraphs: If you're thinking about picking up a MOBA, I'd strongly suggest either muting team chat or queuing with a friend for the first stretch. There is an enormous amount to learn, and you are going to get rolled while you learn it.
But once you're through that first wall and you land the combo exactly the way you pictured it, you'll arrive at the same thought I did: oh no, this game has me.
GuideWhatIsMoba.ctaCompare: Compare: which of the three mobile MOBAs fits you?

definitionBlock.heading: What a MOBA is, in one minute
paragraphs: A MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) is a competitive genre in which two teams of five fight over a single map. Each player controls one character, earns gold, and buys items to grow stronger as the match goes on. The first team to destroy the enemy base (the Nexus, or the Crystal in Honor of Kings) wins. The major titles are all free-to-play.
Match length varies by title. The comparison article puts Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends at 10 to 15 minutes, and Wild Rift at 15 to 20.

On PC the genre is defined by League of Legends (2009) and Dota 2 (2013). On mobile there are the three titles this site covers — Honor of Kings, Wild Rift and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang — alongside Arena of Valor and Pokémon UNITE.

GuideHOK.title: Why We Recommend Honor of Kings: A Thrilling 15-Minute MOBA
GuideHOK.intro: Six months on the global version, from a longtime PC MOBA player. Ultimates unlock in under two minutes and games end in 10 to 15, and that same pace is why an early lead tends to snowball.
GuideHOK.heading: Six Months of Honor of Kings: My Honest Take on the MOBA That Fits After Work
GuideHOK.author: Written by HUB-GAME
leadParagraphs: I have played MOBAs on PC for years, and I walked into this one carrying a bias: a MOBA on a phone means a cramped screen and mushy controls, right?

Then the global version of Honor of Kings reached Japan on June 20, 2024, I gave it a shot, and that bias did not survive the first session. Six months later I still catch myself queuing up "just one more" after work with my brain running on fumes. Here is my honest take on why the pacing works so well.
GuideHOK.tempoHeading: ■ 10 to 15 minutes a match, with no dead air
tempoParagraphs: The pace is the first thing that got me.

In a PC MOBA, the opening ten minutes are usually a patience test: you and your lane opponent quietly last-hitting minions and trading poke. In HoK you hit level 4 in under two minutes and everyone has their ultimate unlocked (as of the August 2026 build).

Movement speed and farming income are tuned to match, so a fight is breaking out somewhere on the map almost from the first minute. There is no lull to sit through, and 10 to 15 minutes is usually enough for one team to push through the towers and close it out.
If you cannot give up 30-plus minutes on a weeknight but still want the tension of a real competitive match, the format lines up with a working adult's schedule almost uncomfortably well.
GuideHOK.controlsHeading: ■ Touch controls that stay out of the way
controlsParagraphs: It is a virtual stick on a phone screen, but the inputs stick where you put them and the response is quick.

Skill aiming is assisted just enough that combos go off in the direction you intended without the game feeling like it is playing for you. It clicks hardest on assassins and mages: dashing behind a squishy target and dumping a full burst combo on them lands closer to an action game than to lane management.

The roster helps too. Heroes drawn from the Three Kingdoms and Chinese mythology — Zhuge Liang, Sun Wukong, Diaochan and the rest — come with loud, colorful spell effects, and simply moving them around the map is satisfying on its own.
downsideParagraphs: It would not be a fair review if I only listed the good parts.

Because matches move fast and gold comes in quickly, the team that builds an early lead tends to snowball straight through to the base. If what you enjoy is the heavier macro game — holding under tower, controlling the map and grinding out a comeback — HoK can feel blunt by comparison.
verdictParagraphs: What kept me coming back for six months is the clock. A game ends in 10 to 15 minutes, so I know when my evening is getting handed back before I ever queue. Ultimates are up inside two minutes, and there is no quiet stretch to sit through.
On a tired weeknight brain, the inputs still go where I aim them. Slipping behind the enemy line on an assassin and landing the whole combo stayed with me whether the game went my way or not.

The speed costs you the comeback. Gold comes in fast, and the team that takes the first lead usually rides it all the way to the base. If the part you enjoy is the heavier macro game — holding the map, grinding an advantage back — this is not the one.
GuideHOK.verdictDataHeading: Honor of Kings by the numbers (as of 2026-08-29)
verdictList: 116 heroes as of 2026-08-29 (Honor of Kings Hub data). Fighters (38) and Mages (37) make up the bulk of the roster, while Tanks (17) and Supports (16) are the thinnest roles.

Patches land every two weeks. The last three hit on July 30, August 13 and August 27, 2026, exactly 14 days apart. The shop holds 114 items, and there are 30 Arcana, ten each in red, blue and green (as of 2026-08-29).

The match runs on a fixed clock. Outer towers take 40% reduced damage for the first four minutes, the Overlord and the Tyrant both spawn at 4:00, and the Tempest Dragon at 20:00. Most games finish well before that, and 20 minutes is about the ceiling (Honor of Kings Hub beginner guide, checked 2026-09-08).
GuideHOK.closing: If you want the tension of a competitive match in a short sitting, Honor of Kings is enough. How it differs from Wild Rift and Mobile Legends is laid out properly in the three-title comparison.
GuideHOK.cta: See tier lists and builds on Honor of Kings Hub

GuideWildRift.title: Wild Rift: Depth and Competitiveness on Mobile
GuideWildRift.intro: A review from someone who spent years on League of Legends on PC. Wild Rift kept warding and last-hitting intact; the price is 15-to-20-minute matches and a lot to learn before you're comfortable.
GuideWildRift.heading: No Compromises: Why Wild Rift Doesn't Play Like a Mobile Game
GuideWildRift.author: Written by HUB-GAME
lead: As someone who spent years on League of Legends on PC, I met the announcement of League of Legends: Wild Rift with equal parts excitement and dread.

There was no way a phone screen could carry League's macro game or the precision that its harder champions demand — that was my assumption going in. Then I actually played it, and what I found was a Summoner's Rift built without shortcuts.
GuideWildRift.section1Heading: ■ Warding and last-hitting made the cut
section1Body: When a MOBA gets streamlined for mobile, the fiddly parts are usually the first to go: wards and vision control disappear, and last-hitting gets automated or flattened into passive gold income.
Wild Rift kept both. Choosing where to drop a ward, and reading when the enemy jungler is about to come out of the fog, is the same mind game it is on PC.

Last-hitting matters just as much — miss the CS and you simply don't get the gold — so every step forward to harass and every step back to hold your spacing in lane still carries weight. That strictness is where the depth comes from, and it's exactly the part other mobile MOBAs tend to sand off.
GuideWildRift.section2Heading: ■ The payoff when your mechanics turn a fight around
section2Body: The controls weren't dumbed down either. The high-skill champions are still genuinely hard to play, and the gap between knowing a combo and landing it is as wide as ever.
Yasuo's dash chains, Zed's shadow-swap combos, Lee Sin's Insec (ward-hop into a Flash kick) — they all made it over, and what your fingers can do translates directly into results.
Sitting on a sliver of HP, dodging a skillshot you saw coming, then Flashing into a combo to turn the kill around: that's a win you know you earned rather than one the game handed you.
GuideWildRift.section3Heading: ■ The honest downsides: a lot to learn, and matches aren't short
section3Body: The flip side of that authenticity is a steep wall for newcomers.

A game usually runs 15 to 20 minutes, and you can't walk away mid-match without leaving four teammates a man down. On top of that there's a mountain to memorize: item builds, what every champion's abilities actually do, and which Dragon buffs your team is stacking.
If you're looking for something you can tap through with half your attention, this probably isn't it.
verdictParagraphs: What you get is a match where the reason you won or lost sits on your side of the screen. Put a ward in the wrong spot and the enemy jungler collects on it; miss the CS and the gold simply isn't there. The fight you turn around counts as something your own hands did.

What you give up is control over your free time. A game runs 15 to 20 minutes, and once it starts you're in it to the end. The list of things to hold in your head keeps growing too: items, what each ability actually does, the Dragon buffs your team is stacking.
If you want to be able to explain a win in your own words, that weight is worth carrying. If low commitment is what matters most to you, Wild Rift isn't the answer.
GuideWildRift.verdictDataHeading: Wild Rift by the numbers (as of 2026-08-26)
recommendedFor: 141 champions as of 2026-08-26 (Wild Rift Hub). Six roles — Fighter, Tank, Mage, Assassin, Marksman and Support — spread across five positions: Top (Solo), Jungle, Mid, Duo (ADC) and Support.

Patches arrive roughly every two weeks. Patch 7.2 landed on July 8, 2026, and 7.2a followed a week later on July 15. From there 7.2b (July 29), 7.2c (August 12) and 7.2d (August 26) came at 14-day intervals. Wild Rift Hub's tier list already applies the 7.2d adjustments, but the statistics behind it were captured on August 25, the day before 7.2d shipped, so the rankings will still move.
GuideWildRift.conclusion: If you want the PC experience on a phone, Wild Rift delivers it. Which of the three suits you is easier to judge with all of them side by side in the comparison article.

GuideCompare.title: Honor of Kings vs Wild Rift vs Mobile Legends: Which Suits You?
GuideCompare.intro: Tempo, objective timers and shop rules across three mobile MOBAs, from someone who plays all of them. Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends run 10 to 15 minutes a game, Wild Rift 15 to 20. Here is how to choose.
GuideCompare.heading: Honor of Kings, Wild Rift or Mobile Legends? An Honest Take on Which to Play
GuideCompare.lead: Honor of Kings (HoK), League of Legends: Wild Rift and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) are the three heavyweights of mobile MOBA. If you are stuck on which one to start with, here is a straight answer from someone who plays all three.

hok.label: Fast, high-tempo matches
hok.name: Honor of Kings
hok.body: Matches run 10 to 15 minutes. You can buy items anywhere on the map, so you spend almost no time away from lane, and teamfights break out early.

wr.label: Deep macro and competition
wr.name: Wild Rift
wr.body: Matches run 15 to 20 minutes. Ward placement and vision control, tight last-hitting, precise mechanics. Built for players who want PC-style depth.

mlbb.label: Light, and driven by the clock
mlbb.name: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang
mlbb.body: Matches run 10 to 15 minutes. Turtle at 2:00, Lord at 8:00. Few timers to learn, and at 339.7 MB the smallest install of the three.

section1.heading: ■ 1. The Real Split: Match Tempo and How Much the Clock Decides
section1.intro: The two biggest differences are how long a match runs and how much of the map is on a fixed timer.
section1.hokBody: Ten to fifteen minutes. The Overlord and the Tyrant both spawn at 4:00, both are replaced by Shadow versions at 10:00, and the Tempest Dragon arrives at 20:00. There is no ward war, and a full teamfight can break out two or three minutes in.
section1.wrBody: Fifteen to twenty minutes. Fog of war is in play, so placing wards to hold vision is not optional. Four elemental dragons, the Rift Herald, Baron and the Elder Dragon come up in turn, which means a longer setup before anything happens.
section1.mlbbBody: Ten to fifteen minutes. The Turtle spawns at 2:00 and the Lord at 8:00, and the shield on the outer turrets drops at five minutes. Three timers, and the call between staying in lane and stepping to the river follows from them.

section2.heading: ■ 2. Shop Rules and Pre-Match Setup
section2.hokBody: You can buy items anywhere on the map without recalling. Unless you are one hit from dying there is no reason to head back, so the game keeps rolling. Arcana fill 10 slots each in red, blue and green, 30 in all, levelled from 1 to 5.
section2.wrBody: Buying items means recalling to the fountain. Reading the lane and picking your moment to reset is itself a skill. Runes come from four trees totalling 53: one keystone plus three minor runes.
section2.mlbbBody: Seven emblems, but the talents are the same on all of them; only the emblem’s own stat line differs. What does bind you is the battle spell: bring Retribution and the only boots you may buy are jungle boots. One pre-match pick sets your shop.

section3.heading: ■ 3. Side by Side, From a Player Perspective

tableRows.mlbb: Light. Objective timers, plus the 22 shop rules behind the item list’s question mark
Built for touch. Ultimates unlock at level 4, so you can commit early

tableRows.hok: Buy anywhere on the map; a recall is for healing
tableRows.wr: Fountain only, so when you reset is a judgement call
tableRows.mlbb: Bring Retribution and only jungle boots are available. Selling returns 60% (30% for advanced boots), or full price in the first 15 seconds

tableRows.wr: Western dark fantasy, the LoL universe
tableRows.mlbb: Myths and heroes from many cultures on one map, from Sun Wukong and Hayabusa to Freya and Lapu-Lapu

tableRows.hok: 116 heroes across six roles: Tank, Fighter, Assassin, Mage, Marksman and Support. 33 of them are listed under two roles.
tableRows.wr: 141 champions across the same six roles: Fighter, Tank, Mage, Assassin, Marksman and Support.
tableRows.mlbb: 133 heroes across the same six roles, with 35 listed under two. Roles and lanes are assigned separately, so one does not imply the other.

tableRows.hok: Five: Clash Lane (solo), Jungle, Mid Lane, Farm Lane and Roam. The roamer has no lane of their own and moves across the whole map.
tableRows.wr: Five: Top (Baron Lane), Jungle, Mid, Duo (Dragon Lane) and Support. Top and Duo sometimes swap lanes after the first turret falls or to set up for an upcoming objective.
tableRows.mlbb: Five: Gold Lane, EXP Lane, Mid Lane, Jungle and Roam. The map has three lanes; jungle and roam are counted alongside them.

tableRows.hok: 114 items in six categories (physical, magic, defense, movement, jungle, roam), with six slots. Every tier-2 boot costs 700G.
tableRows.wr: 167 items including 16 boots. Non-boot items split by price into 12 basic, 43 mid-tier and 96 core, topping out at 3,400G. Six slots, and only one item with an active effect.
tableRows.mlbb: 61 items with six slots. One pair of boots and one active item at a time, and unique passives that share a name do not stack — only the stronger fires.

tableRows.hok: 30 Arcana, 10 each in red, blue and green. You fill 10 slots per color, 30 in total, and level each one from 1 to 5, where the big jump comes at level 5.
tableRows.wr: 53 runes in four trees (Domination, Precision, Resolve, Sorcery): 13 keystones plus 40 minor runes.
tableRows.mlbb: 7 emblems. The talents are identical on every emblem, one from each of three tiers; only the emblem’s own stat line differs.

tableRows.hok: 11 spells with 30-120s cooldowns, unlocked by account level: Sprint at level 1, Flash not until level 19. Jungle items require Smite.
tableRows.wr: 9 spells with 10-150s cooldowns. Smite is the shortest at 10s; Flash and Teleport the longest at 150s. Smite upgrades to Chill Smite after three uses.
tableRows.mlbb: 12 spells, unlocked one at a time by account level. A new account has Retribution and Healing Spell only; Flicker comes at 12 and Purify at 21. Retribution is the price of entry to the jungle.

tableRows.hok: The Overlord and the Tyrant both spawn at 4:00. From 10:00 their Shadow versions take over, and the Tempest Dragon appears at 20:00 with a team-wide shield.
tableRows.wr: Four elemental dragons (Infernal, Ocean, Mountain, Cloud), Rift Herald, Baron Nashor and the late-game Elder Dragon.
tableRows.mlbb: The Turtle spawns at 2:00 and returns two minutes after each kill, stopping at 8:00. The Lord arrives around 8:00 and evolves at 18:00.

tableRows.hok: Roughly every two weeks. In July and August 2026 the updates landed on Jul 2, Jul 16, Jul 30, Aug 13 and Aug 27, 14 days apart. The Season 15 "Grand Venture" update on Jun 17 added four heroes at once.
tableRows.wr: Roughly every two weeks. After 7.2 on Jul 8, patches 7.2a-7.2d followed on Jul 15, Jul 29, Aug 12 and Aug 26. Numbered patches are about three months apart (7.1 on Apr 7, 7.2 on Jul 8); ranked Season 21 opened Apr 10.
tableRows.mlbb: The most recent patch we have verified is 2.1.95 (Aug 26), which adjusted four heroes. Patch notes go up on the official site irregularly; the one before it was 2.1.88 on Jun 17.

tableRows.hok: Developed by TiMi Studio Group, published by Level Infinite (Tencent Games). The global version launched in Japan, North America and Europe on June 20, 2024.
tableRows.wr: Riot Games. Open beta began on October 27, 2020 in Japan, South Korea and Southeast Asia.
tableRows.mlbb: Shanghai Moonton Technology (MOONTON). Published on the Japanese App Store on November 11, 2016, the oldest of the three.

tableRows.hok: 819.1 MB, iOS 12.0 or later. Also on Google Play for Android.
tableRows.wr: 1.1 GB, iOS 15.0 or later. Also on Google Play for Android.
tableRows.mlbb: 339.7 MB, iOS 12.0 or later. Also on Google Play for Android.

section4.heading: ■ 4. Verdict: Which One Is for You

GuideCompare.tableFootnote: Figures for Honor of Kings and Wild Rift are as of August 29, 2026, and for Mobile Legends as of September 9, 2026. Hero, item, arcana/rune/emblem and spell counts come from the data published on each strategy site; patch dates are the publication dates of each game’s official patch notes, except Mobile Legends 2.1.95 which is taken from the in-game notes; app size and OS requirements are as shown on the Japanese App Store.

hok.heading: ▶ Who Honor of Kings Is For
points: • Players with limited free time who want a match wrapped up in 10 to 15 minutes
• Anyone who wants flashy combos and kills without a pile of homework first
• MOBA newcomers who want to pick up the fundamentals while still having fun

wr.heading: ▶ Who Wild Rift Is For
points: • Players who want PC-level tactics and mind games
• Competitive players who want precise skill dodging and vision control to decide the game
• Anyone drawn to the League of Legends world and champion designs

mlbb.heading: ▶ Who Mobile Legends Is For
points: • Players watching their storage: 339.7 MB, the smallest of the three
• Anyone who wants a short list to learn — objective timers and the shop rules cover most calls
• Players who do not mind verifying things themselves, since written coverage is still thin

Quiz.title: Mobile MOBA Aptitude Quiz
Quiz.subtitle: Five questions, then you get which of the three titles fits you and the role to start with.
Quiz.q1: What match tempo do you prefer?
Quiz.q1a1: Fast 10-15 minute games with fighting from the opening minutes
Quiz.q1a2: Slower 15-20 minute games, building an advantage while holding vision
Quiz.q2: How much do you want to set up before a match, and how do you like your controls?
Quiz.q2a1: Let me buy items on the spot. Levelling 30 Arcana slots does not bother me
Quiz.q2a2: Precise play: vision control with wards and dodging skill shots
Quiz.q3: Which art style appeals to you?
Quiz.q3a1: Vibrant Eastern fantasy and historical heroes
Quiz.q4: Where on the map do you want to be fighting?
Quiz.q4a1: On the front line, soaking the enemy's damage so my team can go in
Quiz.q4a2: In the middle, a short walk from every lane so I can dictate the pace
Quiz.q4a3: Nowhere near a lane — roaming the jungle and the enemy's half of the map
Quiz.q4a4: Safe in the backline, dealing damage without getting touched
Quiz.q4a5: Right next to a teammate, scouting ahead and peeling to keep them alive
Quiz.q5: Which kind of win feels best to you?
Quiz.q5a1: Completely shutting down your lane opponent 1v1
Quiz.q5a2: Reading the enemy's next move and collapsing on them first
Quiz.q5a3: Deleting two or three enemies in a single teamfight
Quiz.q5a4: Finishing the game at the top of the damage chart
Quiz.q5a5: Setting your team up so they can commit without hesitating
Quiz.role_hok_top_desc: The clash lane is the island lane: long 1v1s with almost no help, then leading the engage and eating the enemy's opening spells in teamfights. Your answers lean toward handling a situation on your own, and clash is the role that lets you decide when the fight starts.
Quiz.role_wr_top_desc: Top is the island lane: long 1v1s with almost no help, then leading the engage and eating the enemy's opening spells in teamfights. Your answers lean toward handling a situation on your own, and top is the role that lets you decide when the fight starts.
Quiz.role_hok_jungle_desc: Junglers skip laning entirely — you clear camps and pick your own timings for ganks and objectives. You said you win by reading the enemy and hitting first, and jungle is the one role that gets to choose where the fight happens. Jungle items require Smite, and they cut your damage to minions by 25% until the 10:00 mark.
Quiz.role_wr_jungle_desc: Junglers skip laning entirely — you clear camps and pick your own timings for ganks and objectives. You said you win by reading the enemy and hitting first, and jungle is the one role that gets to choose where the fight happens.
Quiz.role_hok_mid_desc: Mid is the shortest walk to every other lane, so you provide damage while setting the tempo of the game. You picked quick, decisive fights and staying involved across the map, which is exactly what mid does once the wave is shoved.
Quiz.role_wr_mid_desc: Mid is the shortest walk to every other lane, so you provide damage while setting the tempo of the game. You picked quick, decisive fights and staying involved across the map, which is exactly what mid does once the wave is shoved.
Quiz.role_hok_adc_desc: Marksmen turn CS into gold and gold into steady damage from the safety of the backline. You chose to farm up and win on raw output, and that patient early game is what the farm lane is trading for. Honor of Kings lets you shop from anywhere, so you can stay in lane for it.
Quiz.role_wr_adc_desc: Marksmen turn last hits (CS) into gold and gold into steady damage from the safety of the backline. You chose to farm up and win on raw output, and that patient early game is what an ADC is trading for.
Quiz.role_hok_support_desc: A roamer buys the Knowledge Gem first, moves across the whole map, soaks the damage meant for the carry and locks enemies down so teammates can commit. You put your team's survival and map information ahead of your own kill count. Honor of Kings has no wards, so vision comes from firing a skill into a bush and watching for a reaction.
Quiz.role_wr_support_desc: Supports buy the wards, take the damage meant for the carry, and lock enemies down so teammates can commit. You put your team's survival and map information ahead of your own kill count, which is the entire job description.
Quiz.shareText: I took the HUB-GAME mobile MOBA quiz — my match is {game} and my best-fit role is {role}.
Quiz.incomplete: Some questions are still unanswered. Fill in the rest, then submit again.
Quiz.pageLead: The title comes from Q1 to Q3. Each answer gives its title the weight of that question: three points for Q1, two each for Q2 and Q3. Split that way, one title always ends up ahead on its own, so a tie cannot happen. The role comes from Q4 and Q5: three points to the role you picked and one to the role beside it, with one more point each from your Q1 and Q2 answers. If two roles still tie, the role you picked yourself in Q4 wins, then Q5.
Quiz.howItWorks: How the quiz scores your answers
Quiz.q1a3: Fast 10-15 minute games where everyone groups on a fixed objective timer
Quiz.q2a3: Keep setup minimal. One emblem and I am ready to play
Quiz.q3a3: Myths and heroes from many cultures sharing one roster
Quiz.result_hok_desc: 10 to 15 minutes per match. You can buy items anywhere on the map, so you spend almost no time away from lane and the pace never drops.
Quiz.result_wr_desc: Vision control with wards and deep laning. Great for players who want to hone real skill.
Quiz.result_mlbb_desc: 10 to 15 minutes per match. Learn the Turtle at 2:00 and the Lord at 8:00 and the early calls follow. At 339.7 MB it is the lightest of the three.
Quiz.role_mlbb_top_desc: The EXP lane is the island lane: you take all the experience there, level fastest, and get the least help. Your answers lean toward handling a situation on your own, which is what a long 1v1 in the EXP lane asks for. The Turtle pit is right beside it, so this is also the lane that can reach the river at 2:00.
Quiz.role_mlbb_jungle_desc: Junglers skip laning entirely and clear camps instead. You said you win by reading the enemy and hitting first, and jungle is the one role that chooses where the fight happens. It requires the battle spell Retribution, which also restricts you to jungle boots. The red and blue buffs run out after 75 seconds, so be in position for the next one before then.
Quiz.role_mlbb_mid_desc: Mid is the short lane in the centre, a step away from either side. You picked quick, decisive fights and staying involved across the map. Shove the wave, then head to the river — do it in the other order and you come back to a chunked turret.
Quiz.role_mlbb_adc_desc: The gold lane pays the most minion gold, so whoever plays it finishes their build first. You chose to farm up and win on raw output, and in the gold lane every last hit turns straight into that. You share the lane with the roamer. The siege minion bonus ends at five minutes, so until then just take the whole wave.
Quiz.role_mlbb_support_desc: Roamers give up farm to hold vision and watch objectives. You put your team’s survival and map information ahead of your own kill count. One roaming item per team is enough, and thriving gold stops accruing at 1,500. For the first eight minutes, farming alone pays only 30%, so stay beside a teammate through that stretch.

Glossary.title: Essential MOBA Glossary
Glossary.description: The basic terms every beginner should know — the shared language of MOBA players.
Glossary.pageLead: The match has already moved on and you still do not know what a gank is. This page is for that. Terms are explained the way Honor of Kings, Wild Rift and Mobile Legends players actually use them, with a note wherever the three games work differently.

Gank.def: Ambushing an enemy from another lane or the jungle to create a numbers advantage. A jungler's main job.

Laning.def: The early phase of the game where you kill minions in your lane to earn experience and gold.
Laning.note: The lane names differ. Wild Rift uses Top (Baron Lane), Mid and Duo (Dragon Lane); Honor of Kings uses Clash Lane (upper), Mid and Farm Lane (lower); Mobile Legends uses EXP Lane (upper), Mid and Gold Lane (lower).

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (lane roles)
Wild Rift Hub: Beginner Guide (lane roles)
MLBB Hub: tier lists by lane

LastHit.def: Dealing the killing blow to a minion to earn gold. The foundation of income — accuracy translates directly into item advantages.
LastHit.note: In Honor of Kings a last hit pays about 1.5x, and items can be bought anywhere on the map. Mobile Legends pays the most in the gold lane, where the siege minion bonus covers only the first ten waves and ends at five minutes. On the Wild Rift side, read this together with the eight wave-management entries.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (last hitting)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (wave management)
MLBB Hub: Gold Lane tier list

Build.def: The order in which you buy items and level skills. Adapting your build to the enemy team is key to winning.
Build.note: Wild Rift has 167 items plus 53 runes, Honor of Kings 114 items plus 30 Arcana, and Mobile Legends 61 items plus 7 emblems. All three give you six slots; in MLBB only one pair of boots and one active item may be held at a time.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Item Build Simulator
Wild Rift Hub: Items
MLBB Hub: item list

BuffDebuff.def: Buffs strengthen (e.g. attack up) and debuffs weaken (e.g. slows). Jungle monster buffs are crucial for early-game control.
BuffDebuff.note: The Honor of Kings red buff applies a slow and true damage, the blue buff 20% cooldown reduction and mana regen, both returning after 90 seconds. Wild Rift grants team-wide buffs from its four dragons. Mobile Legends gives 10% cooldown reduction and 60% cheaper skills on blue, true damage and a slow on red, both lasting 75 seconds.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (Red & Blue Buffs)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (the four dragons)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide

KDA.def: Your kill/death/assist ratio. Beginners improve fastest by focusing on dying less.

Carry.def: The hero your team feeds gold and safe farm so they can win late-game fights. If you are the carry, take the free farm; if you are not, play around protecting the one who is.

Tank.def: A high-health frontliner who starts fights and soaks damage. Tanks buy resistances instead of damage, so judge them by how much enemy attention they pull, not by KDA.

Fighter.def: A melee role that balances durability with damage. Not as tough as a pure tank, but able to hold the front line in a sustained fight. Most play a solo lane — Top in Wild Rift, the Clash Lane in Honor of Kings, the EXP Lane in Mobile Legends.
Fighter.note: The home lane is Top (Baron Lane) in Wild Rift, the Clash Lane in Honor of Kings and the EXP Lane in Mobile Legends. All three are long 1v1s, and in teamfights you either hold the front or flank onto the enemy backline.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Clash Lane Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List (Top)
MLBB Hub: EXP Lane tier list

Assassin.def: A burst hero built to reach the enemy carry and delete them in one combo. Strong when the enemy is split up, near-useless when they group and peel for each other.

Mage.def: A ranged magic-damage hero, usually in the mid lane. Mages jump in strength the moment their first major item completes, so it is worth checking the enemy mage's build before you fight.

Marksman.def: A ranged carry built around basic attacks, scaling hard with items. In Wild Rift they share the Duo (Dragon) lane with a support, and in Mobile Legends the Gold Lane with a roamer. In Honor of Kings they take the Farm Lane, but the roamer has no fixed lane, so a partner is not always beside them.
Marksman.note: Mobile Legends shows this role as Hunter in the Japanese client and as Marksman on the official English site. The Wild Rift ADC farms under a support’s protection, while the Honor of Kings roamer has no fixed lane and moves across the whole map.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Farm Lane Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List (Duo)
MLBB Hub: Gold Lane tier list

Support.def: A role that gives up farm and contributes through vision, crowd control and peel. In Wild Rift they share a lane with the marksman from the start and handle warding. Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends call the role Roam, and it has no fixed lane at all.
Support.note: Wild Rift supports pair with the ADC in the duo lane and hold vision with wards. The Honor of Kings equivalent is Roam, which buys the Gem of Knowledge (300G) and moves across the map. In Mobile Legends one roaming item per team is enough, and thriving gold stops accruing at 1,500.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Roam Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Beginner Guide (support role)
MLBB Hub: Roam tier list

Jungler.def: The player who farms neutral camps instead of a lane and decides where to gank. Their pathing sets the early tempo for the whole team.
Jungler.note: What lets you jungle differs. Honor of Kings requires Smite (1,500 true damage, 30s cooldown) to buy jungle items. Wild Rift deals 600 on a 10s cooldown and upgrades to Chill Smite after three uses. Mobile Legends restricts Retribution holders to jungle boots and cuts damage taken from normal monsters by 40%.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Summoner Spells (Smite)
Wild Rift Hub: Summoner Spells
MLBB Hub: battle spells (Retribution)

Minion.def: The AI soldiers that march down each lane. They are your steady income — clearing waves pays for your build, and shoving them into a tower is how you take it down.
Minion.note: Honor of Kings adds a Ballista from four minutes, and killing the Overlord turns your next two waves into Dragon Vanguards. In Wild Rift, Baron empowers nearby minions. Mobile Legends runs four-minion waves for the first ten, then adds a siege minion after five minutes.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Jungle Boss Guide (Overlord)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Baron Nashor)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide

Recall.def: Channeling back to your fountain to heal and shop. Time it right after you shove the wave in, so you lose the least gold and experience while you are away.
Recall.note: Honor of Kings lets you buy anywhere, so a recall is for healing. In Wild Rift, go before the cannon minion arrives or right after shoving the wave. Mobile Legends puts small healing camps up within 30 to 40 seconds, so health and mana can be reset without going home.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (buy anywhere)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (recall timing)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide

Farm.def: Steadily collecting gold and experience from minions and jungle camps. When a fight is not clearly winnable, taking a wave is usually the higher-value play.

Jungle.def: The neutral area between lanes. Defeat monsters there for experience and buffs.

Bush.def: Grass that hides you from enemy view. A classic spot to ambush the enemy carry.

Tower.def: Lane defenses that hit hard and switch to you the moment you attack an enemy hero in range. Only step in when your own minion wave is there to take the shots for you.
Tower.note: Honor of Kings outer towers take 40% less damage for the first four minutes, and your damage drops 55% with no allied minions beside you. Wild Rift sends the Rift Herald into towers early. Mobile Legends shields its outer turrets for the first five minutes: 30% less damage taken, and 15% less for allies nearby.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (tower protection)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Rift Herald)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide (turret shields)

Nexus.def: The final structure in the enemy base. Wild Rift calls it the Nexus, Honor of Kings the Crystal, and Mobile Legends the Base. Destroy it and the game ends, whatever the kill score says.
Nexus.note: The Honor of Kings Crystal cannot be attacked until a high ground tower falls, and the Mobile Legends Base not until a base turret falls in one of the lanes. In Wild Rift, destroying the third turret in a lane spawns Super Minions there.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (high ground towers)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Inhibitor Turret)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide (base turrets)

Ward.def: An item you place to reveal part of the map. Every Wild Rift player can pick up free wards in the shop, but Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends have no wards at all: vision comes from bushes, the minimap and hero skills.
Ward.note: Wild Rift holds vision with wards and clears the enemy’s with the Sweeping Lens; wards double as teleport anchors. In Honor of Kings the roamer walks into the bush first. In Mobile Legends, stepping into a bush the enemy has no vision of makes you disappear on the spot.

links.label: Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (vision & Sweeping Lens)
Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (vision & bushes)
MLBB Hub: glossary (bushes and vision)

FogOfWar.def: The unlit part of the map where enemies are invisible to you. When an enemy disappears from the minimap, assume they are walking toward you until you see otherwise.

Fountain.def: The healing zone in your base where you shop and refill. Enemies who chase you into it get shredded by the fountain's attack, so a fountain dive is almost never worth it.

Ace.def: Wiping out the entire enemy team. Use the window to take towers and objectives and swing the game.

Peel.def: Protecting your carry (damage dealer) from enemy attacks.

CC.def: Any effect that takes control away from a hero — stun, knock-up, root, silence, slow. Chaining CC is how a team kills a tank, and holding your escape until after the first CC lands is how you survive one.
CC.note: The cleanse spell is Purify in Honor of Kings (120s cooldown), Cleanse in Wild Rift (110s) and Purify in Mobile Legends (unlocks at account level 21). None of them clears suppression.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Summoner Spells (Purify)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (14 crowd-control effects)
MLBB Hub: glossary (suppression and tenacity)

Burst.def: Damage delivered in one short combo rather than over time. Burst heroes live or die on whether the target dies before it can react, so they need setup or CC to land it.

Poke.def: Chipping away at enemy health from outside their range before a fight starts. Enough poke forces the enemy to recall or fight at a health deficit.

Sustain.def: Health you recover on your own — lifesteal, regeneration, or a heal skill. Good sustain lets you stay in lane through poke instead of giving up waves to recall.

Dive.def: Attacking an enemy who is standing under their own tower. It only works when you have a minion wave to hold the tower's aggro and enough damage to finish before it kills you.
Dive.note: Honor of Kings towers take 40% less damage for the first four minutes, so a dive in that window almost never works. Mobile Legends shields its outer turrets for the first five minutes with the same effect. The Wild Rift encyclopedia has an entry on passing tower aggro between allies.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (tower protection)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (tower dive & aggro swap)
MLBB Hub: glossary (turret dive)

Focus.def: Agreeing on one target and killing it first. Damage spread across five enemies kills nobody; five players hitting the same squishy usually decides the fight on the spot.

Kiting.def: Moving between basic attacks so you keep dealing damage while staying out of reach. Attack, step back, attack again — it is the core mechanic of every marksman.

Engage.def: Engage is the skill that starts a fight — a knock-up, a hook, a dash in. Disengage is what pulls your team out of a bad one. Whichever side has the better engage usually gets to choose when the fight happens.

Snowball.def: Turning a small lead into an ever-growing advantage and keeping control of the game.

Push.def: Killing minions to move the front line toward the enemy's towers.

Macro.def: Big-picture strategy: map awareness, objective control, and rotations. Its counterpart, micro, refers to mechanical skill.

Objective.def: A neutral monster that grants a powerful team-wide buff. Fights over the Wild Rift dragons and Baron, the Honor of Kings Tyrant and Overlord, and the Mobile Legends Turtle and Lord decide most matches.
Objective.note: In Honor of Kings the Overlord and Tyrant spawn at 4:00 and the Tempest Dragon at 20:00. Wild Rift has seven: four dragons, the Herald, Baron and Elder. Mobile Legends runs the Turtle from 2:00 until 8:00, then the Lord from 8:00, which evolves at 18:00.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Jungle Boss Guide (Tyrant & Overlord)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (all 7 objectives)
MLBB Hub: beginner guide (Turtle and Lord)

Roam.def: Leaving your lane to gank, contest an objective or hold vision. Shove the wave before you move and you lose no farm doing it. In Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends it is also the name of the supporting position.
Roam.note: In Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends it is a role, and both sites split their tier lists by it. The Mobile Legends roamer earns only 30% from minions and camps killed alone during the first eight minutes. In Wild Rift the word describes an action only.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Roam Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (Roam)
MLBB Hub: Roam tier list

SplitPush.def: Pushing a side lane alone while your team holds the enemy's attention elsewhere. It forces them to send someone to answer, which is how you create the numbers fight your team can win.
SplitPush.note: Honor of Kings has a warp point on the clash side (usable once the sprite is killed, 30s reuse) that makes regrouping fast. The Wild Rift encyclopedia covers the 1-4 and 1-3-1 formations. In Mobile Legends, taking one base turret means that lane spawns Super Minions for the rest of the game.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (warp point)
Wild Rift Hub: Glossary (1-4 and 1-3-1 split push)
MLBB Hub: glossary (super minions)

WaveManagement.def: Controlling where the minion waves meet. Freeze the wave near your own tower to farm safely, or slow push a big wave first so you have time to take an objective.

Scaling.def: How much stronger a hero gets from levels and items. A late-scaling team should trade early aggression for farm; an early-game team has to convert its lead before the other side catches up.

PowerSpike.def: The moment a hero jumps in strength — a key level or a completed item. Look for fights right after your own spike, and avoid them right after the enemy's.
PowerSpike.note: Honor of Kings and Mobile Legends both unlock ultimates at level 4, which is the first spike. The Mobile Legends EXP laner takes all the lane experience and arrives there first. In Wild Rift, tier-3 boots unlock at 10:00, so your earlier boot choice sets up the late game.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Beginner's Guide (game flow)
Wild Rift Hub: Items (boots)
MLBB Hub: EXP Lane tier list

Meta.def: The heroes, builds and strategies that are strongest under the current patch. It shifts with every balance change, so check the patch date on any tier list you read.
Meta.note: The tier lists draw on official win, pick and ban rates: in-game HoK Camp for Honor of Kings, the Chinese server statistics (Master and above) for Wild Rift, and the official Hero Ranking for Mobile Legends, covering the past seven days in the Mythic bracket.

links.label: Honor of Kings Hub: Tier List
Wild Rift Hub: Tier List
MLBB Hub: current tier list

About.title: About
About.siteText: HUB-GAME (hub-game.com) is a strategy portal focused on mobile MOBAs. This site offers comparison articles, an aptitude quiz, and a glossary to help you choose a title, while our sister sites cover detailed strategy for Honor of Kings, Wild Rift and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang. The Mobile Legends site is published in Japanese only.
About.operatorText: HUB-GAME team (email: contact@hub-game.com / X: @hub_gamecom). The articles and data are produced by an operator who plays Honor of Kings, Wild Rift and Mobile Legends daily, working from hands-on play and the actual in-game screens.
About.policyText: Articles are based on what we have verified through actual play. Because patches make information go stale, we note the verification date for numbers and balance claims wherever possible. Anything we cannot confirm is marked as unverified rather than guessed. If you spot an error, please let us know via the contact page.
About.contactText: For questions, information, or feedback about our content, please see the contact page.
methodList: Hero base stats and skill numbers are transcribed from screenshots of the actual game screens. For Honor of Kings, we cross-checked 113 hero stat screens plus 140 skill and item detail screens in August 2026.

Win, pick, and ban rates on the tier lists come from official statistics (HoK Camp for Honor of Kings), fetched manually, with the retrieval date shown on the page. They are not always current, so check the date before you rely on them.
Before publishing, the Japanese and English data sets are compared mechanically so that an outdated value cannot survive in only one language.
Where the comparison article or the glossary describes how the games differ, the figures are the same ones published on each strategy site, with the verification date attached.

GuideTermMapping.title: Mobile MOBA Term Map and Switching Guide
GuideTermMapping.intro: Twenty-three things Honor of Kings, Wild Rift and Mobile Legends all have but call by different names, lined up side by side — each with a one-line note on how the mechanics actually differ, from spawn timers to what you are allowed to buy.
GuideTermMapping.lead: Crystal, Nexus and Base. Tyrant, Dragon and Turtle. Arcana, Runes and Emblems. The names differ, but the job each one does in a match is close to identical. Treat them as the same thing, though, and the details — spawn times, how shopping works — will trip you up. Drawing on the glossaries of our three strategy sites, this page pairs up the terms and notes where the mechanics diverge.

sections.heading: Map and Base
sections.intro: All three maps run three lanes plus a jungle. What changes is what the base is called and how the lanes are named.

rows.note: Destroying it ends the game in all three. HoK requires you to bring down a high ground tower first, and MLBB a base turret in one of the lanes, before the final structure can be attacked.
All three spawn Super Minions in that lane once destroyed. MLBB gives each team nine turrets in three tiers: outer, inner and base.

rows.wr: Baron Lane (listed as "Top" on Wild Rift Hub)
rows.note: A fighter or tank 1v1 in all three. In MLBB the Turtle pit sits right beside it, and only this lane and the jungler can reach the river by 2:00.

rows.wr: Dragon Lane ("Duo" on Wild Rift Hub)
rows.note: A ranged carry plus a support in all three. MLBB’s gold lane pays the most minion gold, and the siege minion bonus runs out at five minutes.
Every Wild Rift player carries a free ward, and where you place it is a mind game. HoK and MLBB rely on bushes: step into one the enemy has no vision of and you vanish on the spot.

sections.heading: Objectives and Buffs
sections.intro: The moment the teams first group up differs across the three. Even when a boss plays the same role, the reward takes a different shape.

rows.note: Tyrant gives everyone Chain Lightning on their attacks. Wild Rift’s dragons each buff a different team-wide stat. The Turtle pays gold, experience and a shield to the whole team, with an extra stat bonus for whoever lands the last hit.

Overlord turns your next two waves into Dragon Vanguards. The Herald charges a turret once the Eye is used. The Lord marches with you and hits the first turret it meets for 30% of its maximum health as true damage.
At 10:00 both HoK bosses are replaced by their Shadow versions. Baron appears from the mid game on and grants Hand of Baron: more AD/AP and heavily empowered nearby minions.

rows.mlbb: Red buff (Molten Fiend) / Blue buff (Thunder Fenrir)
rows.note: MLBB’s buffs last 75 seconds and return 90 seconds after being killed. Blue cuts all cooldowns by 10% and mana costs by 60%. Red adds true damage and a slow, which reaches 60% for melee heroes.

Tempest shields every living teammate for 20–50% of max HP. Elder makes your attacks execute enemies below a health threshold. In MLBB, losing a base turret means that lane spawns Super Minions for the rest of the game.

sections.heading: Progression: Items, Arcana/Runes/Emblems, Spells
sections.intro: Pre-game setup follows different logic in all three, and once the match starts the biggest gap is where and what you are allowed to buy.

rows.note: Arcana are fixed bonuses slotted 10 each in red, blue and green, 30 in total. Runes come from four trees as a keystone plus minor runes. Emblems number seven, but the talents are identical on all of them: one from each of three tiers.

rows.concept: Shared skills picked before the match
rows.hok: Battle Spells (Summoner Spells on the HoK Hub list page)
rows.note: HoK has 11, Wild Rift 9 and MLBB 12. HoK and MLBB unlock them one at a time by account level. Names can match while the numbers do not, as the next three rows show.
HoK’s Flash does not unlock until account level 19. Until then you use Sprint, which is available from level 1.

HoK deals 1,500 true damage with a 1s stun, and without it you cannot buy jungle items. Wild Rift deals 600 and heals off monsters. MLBB’s Retribution restricts you to jungle boots, and skipping it locks jungle boots out entirely.
None of them clears suppression. In MLBB, suppression stops movement, skills, basic attacks and battle spells alike, and tenacity does not shorten it.

HoK lets you swap boots for free after a five-minute cooldown. Wild Rift upgrades from 400G boots to tier 2, with tier 3 unlocking at 10:00. In MLBB the battle spell you bring decides which type you may buy, and advanced boots sell back for only 30%.

sections.heading: Roles and Lanes
sections.intro: HoK calls them heroes and Wild Rift champions, but the five roles line up closely. "Roam" is a role name in HoK and MLBB, while in Wild Rift it describes an action.

rows.note: HoK roamers buy the Gem of Knowledge (300G) first and move across the whole map. Wild Rift supports stand beside the marksman and hold vision with wards. MLBB needs only one roaming item per team, and thriving gold stops accruing at 1,500.
The job is the same. MLBB shows the role as Hunter in the Japanese client and as Marksman on the official English site. HoK lets you shop on the spot, so staying in lane is easier.

HoK jungle items require Smite and cut your minion damage by 25% until 10:00. MLBB’s Retribution cuts damage taken from normal monsters by 40%, and for the first two minutes you do not share minion bonuses with allies.

sections.heading: Match Flow and Vocabulary
sections.intro: Match length and the ultimate unlock level differ, so the same word for "early game" points at a different stretch of the clock.

rows.note: HoK lets you buy anywhere, so recalling is almost purely for health. Wild Rift confines shopping to the fountain, which makes the timing a skill. MLBB has small healing camps up within 30 to 40 seconds, so you can reset health and mana without going home.

HoK reaches level 4 in under two minutes and the Tempest Dragon at 20:00. Wild Rift’s first marker is the Herald at 6:00, so everything runs later. MLBB groups up earliest of the three, at the 2:00 Turtle.
HoK and MLBB both open at level 4, which is the first window to commit. Wild Rift unlocks at 5 and upgrades at 9 and 13. MLBB’s EXP laner takes all the lane experience, so they arrive there first.

HoK pays roughly 1.5x what a minion dying beside you pays. Wild Rift punishes missed CS heavily. MLBB’s gold lane pays the most, and the siege minion bonus covers only the first ten waves, ending at five minutes.

switchGuide.heading: Habits to Break When You Switch

hok.heading: Coming from Honor of Kings
body: Shopping is what catches you first. Wild Rift sells only at the fountain, so gold in your pocket buys nothing where you stand. Get into the habit of shoving the wave before you recall.
Vision changes too. Every Wild Rift player carries a free ward, and where you place it is a mind game. Enemy wards come down with the Sweeping Lens.
Reset your sense of time. In HoK 4:00 means two objectives at once; Wild Rift’s Herald is at 6:00 and MLBB’s Turtle at 2:00. The first group-up lands at a different point in each.

wr.heading: Coming from Wild Rift
body: The first task is to stop pausing to shop. In HoK, gold can be spent while you are walking or even dead. Treat the recall as a heal and the tempo starts to make sense.
Switch to playing without wards. In both HoK and MLBB you throw a skill into a bush before entering and read the reaction. If an enemy drops off the minimap, assume they are coming for you.
Objectives arrive early in both. HoK puts the Overlord and Tyrant at 4:00 and swaps in Shadow versions at 10:00. MLBB’s Turtle is at 2:00, and only the EXP laner and jungler can get there.

mlbb.heading: Coming from Mobile Legends
body: Your timers will be wrong. The equivalent of the 2:00 Turtle is the Overlord and Tyrant at 4:00 in HoK, and the Rift Herald at 6:00 in Wild Rift.
Pre-game setup gets heavier. MLBB gives every emblem the same talents, while HoK asks you to fill 30 Arcana slots and Wild Rift to build runes from four trees totalling 53.
Your shop opens up. In MLBB, Retribution decides your boots. HoK sells every tier-2 boot at 700G and lets you swap free after five minutes; Wild Rift unlocks tier 3 at 10:00.

GuideTermMapping.closing: Figures for Honor of Kings and Wild Rift are as of 2026-08-29, and for Mobile Legends as of 2026-09-09. All of them move with patches, so when in doubt check the glossary and boss pages on each site.

GuideMLBB.title: Mobile Legends Review: Three Timers and a 339 MB Download
GuideMLBB.intro: A review of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, live since 2016. The Turtle at 2:00 and the Lord at 8:00 decide most of your calls, and one emblem is all the pre-match setup you need. The thin English and Japanese coverage is covered honestly too.
GuideMLBB.heading: Learn Three Timers and Your Calls Change: Inside Mobile Legends
GuideMLBB.author: Written by HUB-GAME
lead: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) went live on the Japanese App Store on November 11, 2016. Among mobile MOBAs it is one of the oldest still running.
Set beside the other two titles, there is less to memorise. What you do need is the clock: knowing when things spawn changes what you should be doing.
GuideMLBB.section1Heading: ■ The clock makes most of your decisions
section1Body: The Turtle first spawns at 2:00. Kill it and another arrives two minutes later, until the spawns stop at 8:00. The first one always appears on the EXP lane side of the river.
Only the EXP laner and the jungler can reach the river by 2:00. Whether those two have shoved their wave decides who takes the first objective.
Outer turrets carry a golden shield for the first five minutes. The turret takes 30% less damage and allies standing near it take 15% less. Before five minutes, they are not coming down.

The Lord arrives around 8:00, two minutes after the last Turtle dies. Kill it and it marches with you, hitting the first turret it meets for 30% of that turret’s maximum health as true damage. It evolves at 18:00.
Those three timers are enough to answer the only question that matters early: stay in lane, or step to the river.
GuideMLBB.section2Heading: ■ There is very little to set up before a match
section2Body: There are seven emblems. The talents you can pick are the same on all of them, and what differs is the stat line the emblem itself carries. Every emblem takes one talent from each of the three tiers.

So whichever one you level, your options stay the same. Next to building runes from four trees in Wild Rift, or filling 30 Arcana slots in Honor of Kings, there is barely anything to do before the match starts.

There are 61 items. Selling returns 60% of what you paid, and advanced boots only 30%. For the first 15 seconds of a match, though, anything sells for full price, so a misclick can be undone on the spot.

One pre-match choice does bind your shop. Bring the battle spell Retribution and the only boots you may buy are jungle boots; leave it at home and jungle boots are locked out. You decide whether you are jungling before the game begins.
GuideMLBB.section3Heading: ■ The honest downside: coverage is thin
section3Body: There is far less written about MLBB than about the two newer titles, in English and in Japanese. Even hero name spellings are not settled everywhere.
The in-game text and the official site do not always agree either. The ranged carry role is shown as Hunter in the Japanese client and as Marksman on the official English site.

The official data assigns each hero six possible roles and five possible lanes separately. Of the 133 heroes, 35 carry two roles, and some are listed under two lanes. Knowing the role does not tell you the lane.

Roamers have a rule that catches people out: for the first eight minutes, killing minions or jungle camps alone pays only 30%. Farm on your own without knowing that and eight minutes pass with nothing to show.
verdictParagraphs: What you get is a game that pays back the little it asks you to learn. Three timers cover the early calls. One emblem covers the pre-match setup.
What you take on is checking things yourself. The written coverage is thin and the naming is inconsistent, which is why this site transcribes what the client actually shows.
If storage matters, there is one more reason. The Japanese App Store lists it at 339.7 MB, against 1.1 GB for Wild Rift and 819.1 MB for Honor of Kings.
GuideMLBB.verdictDataHeading: Mobile Legends by the numbers (as of September 9, 2026)
recommendedFor: 133 heroes across six roles: Tank, Fighter, Assassin, Mage, Marksman and Support, with 35 of them listed under two roles. Five lanes: Gold, EXP, Mid, Jungle and Roam.
61 items, 7 emblems and 12 battle spells. Battle spells unlock one at a time with account level, and a new account has two of them.
The most recent patch we have verified is 2.1.95 (August 26, 2026), which adjusted four heroes.
The Japanese App Store lists 339.7 MB, iOS 12.0 or later. First published on November 11, 2016 by MOONTON.
GuideMLBB.conclusion: Light to install, light to learn, and clear about what decides a fight. Whether it suits you better than Honor of Kings or Wild Rift is easier to judge with all three side by side in the comparison article.
